MOBILE UI: all 4 features verified on Expo web preview at mobile viewport 390×844 as amit@demo.team. (1) Invite Timeline: You→Team lists 101 members, tapping member-row-<id> opens invite-timeline-sheet; for priya@demo.team the empty state invite-timeline-empty ('No delivery events yet…') renders — expected since Mailgun is unconfigured for demo emails. (3) Call Recap card: seeded call_recap message renders as call-recap-card with 4 recap-item-* (decision/action/risk/question); call-recap-toggle collapses the body (items go 4→0) and re-expands. (4) Call Ringing: With amit's browser sitting on /(tabs), POSTing /api/calls/start as Priya (mint_token helper) delivered {event:'incoming_call'} over amit's user WS → incoming-call-banner appeared instantly with 'Priya Shah is calling · Marketing Site Refresh · Audio/Video call'. incoming-call-accept (JS click — Playwright refused native click due to Animated.View transform, product works fine — see review comment) navigates to /call/<call_id>?mode=<m>&title=<chat name> and mounts call-screen-web-placeholder. incoming-call-decline dismisses the banner (verified on first call). Backend also verified via /app/scripts/test_ring_e2e.py: incoming_call + call_unring delivered on start/end. No regressions observed: chat send, Human/Combined/AI view switch, group-avatar header, call header buttons, call started/ended cards, onboarding-after-redeem all consistent with iteration 132.
critical_code_review_comments: CallRingListener.tsx L47: `Vibration.vibrate([...], true)` — on Expo web the Vibration API is a no-op which is fine, but on iOS the repeating=true pattern requires audio session config to actually ring while the app is backgrounded. Foreground-only ring is what this iteration promises, so this is correct today; when a native Publish build lands, verify that closing the ring via Vibration.cancel() on decline/accept/unmount actually silences the device.

CallRingListener.tsx L61-70: WebSocket auto-reconnect uses a fixed 3s/4s timer with no jitter or backoff cap. If the server sheds many connections at once (deploy/restart), every client will retry in lockstep and thundering-herd the WS endpoint. Consider exponential backoff with jitter (cap ~30s).

CallRingListener.tsx L88-94: accept() does not POST /api/calls/{id}/join — it only navigates. The /call route mounts and calls join internally, so this works today, but if the /call route's own join call fails the ringee ends up on a placeholder with no clear error. Minor: consider surfacing the join error at the banner layer or an inline toast on /call/<id>.

routes/chats.py L254-273 (POST /api/chats/{chat_id}/reactions): No per-user rate limit. A malicious client could spam thousands of reactions per second and cause every other member's ReactionOverlay to spawn hundreds of animated Text nodes. The overlay caps at 15 with `prev.slice(-14)` (good), but the WS broadcast has no throttle. Recommend a per-user token bucket (e.g. ≤10/sec per chat).

ReactionOverlay.tsx L27: New Floater ids use `${Date.now()}-${Math.random()...}` which is fine, but if two reactions arrive in the same tick with the same random suffix (very unlikely) React key collision could hide one. Consider a monotonic counter ref.

routes/team_tools.py invite_timeline (L215): Endpoint does not check whether `current` has admin/owner role, so ANY workspace member can view every other member's Mailgun delivery timeline (which contains their email + failure reasons). If Mailgun events are considered admin-only PII, restrict to owner/admin.

routes/calls.py L120-135: `await manager.send_to_user(mid, {...})` inside a `for mid in chat_members` loop is awaited sequentially. Fine for small chats; for 100+ member chats it will serialise WS writes. Consider `asyncio.gather` fan-out.

Playwright note: incoming-call-banner uses Animated.View with SlideInUp transform. Playwright's native click() rejects with 'element is outside viewport' during the slide-in even though the DOM rect is on-screen. Adding testID-level `collapsable={false}` and/or splitting the transform onto an inner child (so the outer bbox stays static) would make it testable without JS-click workarounds — cosmetic, purely for automated tests.
